"And after the league made with him he shall work deceitfully: for he shall come up, and shall become strong with a small people" [23].

At first Antiochus was despised in Syria, and there were attempts, supported by Egypt, for the lawful king "the son of Seleucus" to take the rule. But Antiochus sent to the king of Egypt (his sister's son) asking for his friendship, especially as Cleopatra, the sister of Antiochus, was still alive. Ptolemy was reassured by his uncle Antiochus and they became friends, but when Antiochus had established his footing he suddenly launched a campaign of a small number and seized some cities of Egypt from his nephew, who did not expect this campaign.
"He shall enter suddenly upon the fattest places of the land; and he shall do that which his fathers have not done, nor his fathers' fathers;
he shall scatter among them the prey, and spoil, and riches: yea, and he shall forecast his devices against the strong holds, even for a time" [24].

By his deceit, and not by a huge military force, he was able to seize some of his cities from his nephew and plunder them and carry spoil and wealth to his country, since the Egyptians lived in luxury. Antiochus went back thinking how he would afterward attack the fortified land of Egypt as a second stage.

Antiochus surpassed his fathers and forefathers in deceit, and there was none to compare with him, especially as the breaking of covenants - especially in the East - is considered shameful, whatever the circumstances.

"And he shall stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall be stirred up to battle with a very great and mighty army; but he shall not stand: for they shall forecast devices against him" [25].

After seizing the open, secure cities and plundering them, Antiochus went back to prepare a huge army to conquer Egypt and attack its fortified cities. He needed a long time to form this army after having seized many neighboring countries by his deceit. At the same time his nephew perceived his uncle's inclinations, so he prepared for open battle and equipped himself with a great army. [21-25] focused on Antiochus Epiphanes, who was referred to before in chapter 8, and who was called "the Antichrist of the Old Testament period".

The men of his palace called him Epiphanes, that is, the exalted or the glorious, because he was concerned with the arts and architecture and with building huge, beautiful, and glorious edifices, but some changed one letter, Epimanes, which means "the madman", because he was violent, deceitful, and deranged in his conduct.
"Yea, they that feed of the portion of his meat shall destroy him, and his army shall overflow: and many shall fall down slain" [26].
God permitted Ptolemy to be defeated before Antiochus through the betrayal of his men, because he was absorbed in pleasures, covetous, and heedless of the affairs of his country.
"And both these kings' hearts shall be to do mischief, and they shall speak lies at one table; but it shall not prosper: for yet the end shall be at the time appointed" [27].

The two kings, the uncle and his nephew, were wicked and deceitful, so when Ptolemy was broken the two saw their need of reconciliation and of entering into friendship, so that each might plan for the other what would destroy him. Antiochus had defeated his nephew but did not dare to complete the journey, for he feared collapse before the rest of the fortified cities. The two sat at one table, but their hearts were full of hatred and enmity. Thus politics does to many, so that a person loses his trust in those nearest to him.

The angel says: "for yet the end shall be at the time appointed" [27], meaning that what happened was within certain limits, so that God's plan might be fulfilled, for the end had not yet come, but God has appointed a time for everything.
"Then shall he return into his land with great riches; and his heart shall be against the holy covenant; and he shall do exploits, and return to his own land" [28].

Antiochus returned to his land, Syria, and did not possess Egypt, but he carried much wealth from it, then returned to wage war against Jerusalem and the holy Temple, and against all the Jews. He was compelled to leave Jerusalem, as he left many treasuries, as it is written in (2 Macc 5:2), where God wrought wonders. He added what he had seized from the Temple to what he had plundered from Egypt, and returned to Syria carrying within him the desire to resist the holy covenant, that is, to resist God Himself.
"At the time appointed he shall return, and come toward the south; but it shall not be as the former, or as the latter.

For the ships of Chittim shall come against him: therefore he shall despair, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant" [29-30].

When the treaty was made between Antiochus and his nephew and they sat together at one table, without cause Antiochus prepared his army and broke the covenant and entered Egypt and seized part of it, and he besieged Alexandria and took the boy king captive. At that time a Roman mission came headed by Publuis or Popilus from Chittim, by which is meant Macedonia, Greece, and Italy. Antiochus received him very kindly as was his custom, but Publius was not deceived; rather he demanded of him, by order of the council of the Senators or Roman elders, that he leave Egypt at once. He asked him for a delay to consult with his friends and advisers, but Publius firmly drew a circle around the king with the staff in his hand, and asked him to call his advisers and come to an understanding with them at once before going out of the circle, or else he would declare war against him immediately. Antiochus could not hesitate, but surrendered himself into the hands of the Senator and turned back from Egypt. This historical fact the angel declared to Daniel the prophet.

Antiochus did not achieve his ambitions in Egypt, and returned in shame merely at a word from the Roman Senator, so he turned back to direct all his energies against Jerusalem and the holy Temple; this time he came to Jerusalem more violently and fiercely than the previous time. He went back seeking traitors to the Temple, among the Jews, who "forsake the holy covenant", to use them against the Jewish people and the divine holy things. This was fulfilled as is described in detail in (2 Macc 3-5).
"And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate" [31].
The arms that stood in support of Antiochus are those who betrayed God and forgot the Law, so they were supporters of the wicked king against divine truth (2 Macc 4).
The Jews wrongly heard that Antiochus had been killed and rejoiced greatly, and when he heard of the matter on his way back he passed through Jerusalem and dealt with them very harshly.

The Jews took refuge in Rome for support, so Rome sent an army while Antiochus turned to resist the Jewish forces under the leadership of the Maccabees [29]. Antiochus submitted to Rome and promised to keep the peace, but as soon as the Roman forces returned he betrayed the promise [30], and some traitors from the Jews helped him in that.

With his known deceit he did not prevent the worship of the living God, but he began first by practicing pagan worship inside the Temple side by side with the worship of God. He defiled the Temple by placing in it the statue of Jupiter Olympius, then afterward he stopped the Jewish worship, set himself up as a god, and sacrificed a pig on the altar. The faithful pious rose up against him under the leadership of the heroic family of the Maccabees, and thousands of them were killed. What he did is reckoned "the abomination of desolation of the Temple", a type of the abomination of desolation that will occur at the end of the ages, to which the Lord Christ referred (Mt 25:24).
"And such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he corrupt by flatteries:
but the people that do know their God shall be strong, and do exploits" [32].

The angel makes clear how the priests and also the people were divided into two groups, one group deceived by the flatteries of Antiochus, and another who held fast to the knowledge of God, so God grants them more strength and understanding. As St. Jerome says: [No one doubts that this will also happen in the days of the Antichrist, when many will resist him and flee from him in many directions. The Jews interpret these things as concerning the destruction of the Temple at the hands of Vespasian and Titus, and they say that many of those whom he raised up knew their Lord and were killed for keeping His Law].

St. Jerome says: [We read in the Maccabees that there were those who pretended to be guardians of the Law of God, and finally entered into a covenant with the Gentiles... But in my opinion this will happen in the days of the Antichrist when the love of many will grow cold. Of these our Lord says in the Gospel, "Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?" (Lk 18:8)].
"And they that understand among the people shall instruct many:
and they glory in the sword, and in flame, in captivity, and in spoil, many days.
Now when they shall fall, they shall be holpen with a little help: but many shall cleave to them with flatteries" [33-34].

The wise among the people (probably of the priests) rejected the flatteries of Antiochus and taught many to despise all means of torment, whether killing by the sword or burning with fire or their captivity or the plundering of their possessions, reckoning all these as glories and honor.

Here is a call to follow the loyal and the faithful in their relationship with God, and not to be led after flatterers whatever their rank or position. It is also a call to the priests and leaders to accept the sword and despise the fire, and not to lose their loyalty to God and their adherence to the divine commandment, for even if they seem to have fallen, and there is no help but a little, like the Maccabees to whom only a very few faithful clung, they must not care about temporal glories and praise.
"And some of them of understanding shall fall, to try them, and to purge, and to make them white, even to the time of the end:
because it is yet for a time appointed" [35].

Here he affirms that some of the understanding will fall, and perhaps he means here falling by the sword or by burning with fire, but this does not mean that God does not support them; rather He permits this for their salvation, for their approval in the end, where they are purged and made white by the work of God in them during their suffering in tribulation. They are counted martyrs who passed through the fires and were refined like pure gold.

Thus God was preparing the souls of the Maccabees and those like them not from the moment of their birth, but even before their creation... so that when they moved to action and saw the resistance, they would return to the prophecies of Daniel and be strengthened and not fear.

St. Hippolytus of Rome says: [Antiochus became king over Syria, reigning in the year 107 of the kingdom of Greece. At the same time he stirred up war against Ptolemy king of Egypt, defeated him, and gained dominion. On his return from Egypt he went up to Jerusalem in the year 103, carrying with him all the treasures of the house of the Lord, and headed to Antioch. After two years the king sent a collector of taxes to the cities of Judea to compel the Jews to abandon the laws of their fathers and subject them to the statutes of the king. He came and tried to compel them to this, saying: "Come forth, and do the commandments of the king, and you shall live." But they answered: "We will not come forth, nor will we do the king's commandments; we shall die pure"; so he slew a thousand souls (1 Macc 2:33). Thereby was fulfilled what Daniel said: "and they shall stumble by toils and famine and sword and captivity" (Dan 11:33). And Daniel adds: "they shall be holpen with a little help" (Dan 11:34). For Mattathias arose at that time, and Judas Maccabeus, to help them and deliver them from the hands of the Greeks].
Suddenly the vision turned to the end of times and the coming of the Antichrist, in a detailed account of his person and his wicked works.

entries.section: 4. The end of times - the Antichrist:

paragraphs.text: 36 And the king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvellous things against the God of gods, and shall prosper till the indignation be accomplished: for that that is determined shall be done. 37 Neither shall he regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god: for he shall magnify himself above all. 38 But in his estate shall he honour the God of forces: and a god whom his fathers knew not shall he honour with gold, and silver, and with precious stones, and pleasant things. 39 Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god: whoso knoweth him he shall increase with glory, and he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for a reward. 40 And at the time of the end shall the king of the south push at him: and the king of the north shall rise up against him with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall enter into the countries, and shall overflow and pass through. 41 He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many shall stumble: but these shall escape out of his hand, even Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon. 42 He shall stretch forth his hand also upon the countries: and the land of Egypt shall not escape. 43 But he shall have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt: and the Libyans and the Ethiopians shall be at his steps. 44 But tidings out of the east and out of the north shall trouble him: therefore he shall go forth with great fury to destroy, and utterly to make away many. 45 And he shall plant the tabernacles of his palace between the seas and the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and none shall help him. [36-39] presents the same person mentioned in (Dan 7:8; 9:26) as the "little horn"; here he calls him the king who does according to his will [36].

"And the king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvellous things against the God of gods, and shall prosper till the indignation be accomplished: for that that is determined shall be done.
Neither shall he regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god: for he shall magnify himself above all" [36-37].

The Jews differed in their interpretation of the preceding text; some thought that the angel is speaking of Antiochus Epiphanes, and others thought that the talk here is about the Romans such as Vespasian and his son Titus, or the Roman state as a whole. But the Fathers of the Church saw that the talk here is about the Antichrist and not about Antiochus, because what follows does not apply to him. Yet some saw that the talk is about the arrogant Roman state, in which some emperors set themselves up as gods and demanded that the people bow down to their statues and images.

This person, who walks by his own will, places himself above everything like Lucifer (Isa 14:13-14), even above God Himself. He represents the glorification of the self, which the Christian faith resists.

He ascribes to himself divine honors and utters wonders (blasphemies) against God, the God of gods. Since it is said that he regards not the God of his fathers, some have been led to say that the Antichrist will be a Jew who renounces the faith.
What is stated here about the Antichrist, that he is a ruler who restores the Roman state and that he resists the Jews, has made some think that he is a Christian who renounces the faith.

The Hebrew word for "the God of his fathers" is Elohim, which is also translated "gods"; thus it is thought that he despises all the religions of his fathers. The only god he believes in is power and violence, the god of military might.

As for "the desire of women", as St. Jerome says: [There are two interpretations of this expression: either that it means seeking the desire of women or renouncing this desire, as the Antichrist will do, who will pretend to chastity in order to deceive many. Some see that it refers here to the desire of Jewish women to conceive the Messiah. And perhaps it means that he cares nothing for women and their desires. It is said that Hitler was of this kind. In the sixteenth century there were two opinions, which Calvin rejected; the first is that what is meant here is "the Pope", for in chapter seven of the first volume of the Councils the canons of Pope Siricius say that those who are in the flesh cannot please God, reckoning that marriage is close to fornication. The second opinion is the desire for women, where a person is permitted to be joined legally to more than one wife. And some see that the talk here is about the Roman emperors who were famous for their hatred of their wives and of the female sex in general.

St. Jerome says: [The text here applies to the Antichrist and not to Antiochus, because the latter tried to compel the Jews and the Samaritans to keep feasts for his gods, and he set up statues of the Greek gods; but the Antichrist cares nothing for the gods of his fathers, but sets himself up as God.
"But in his estate shall he honour the God of forces: and a god whom his fathers knew not shall he honour with gold, and silver, and with precious stones, and pleasant things.
Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god:

entries.section: 4. The end of times - the Antichrist:

paragraphs.text: whoso knoweth him he shall increase with glory, and he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for a reward" [38-39].

He speaks here about the "Antichrist", the god whom his fathers knew not, and he means "himself", for he ascribes to himself divine honors, and demands all wealth and authority for himself; he is the strange god. And he will give gifts to those who submit to him and are deceived by him.

Some see that this applies also to the Roman state, which rejected the worship of the living God, and whose god was power and impregnable fortresses, and the love of authority along with the demanding of tribute and material gains from the states it colonized. The emperors set up for themselves or for their gods statues of gold, silver, precious stones, and costly things. They reckoned themselves greater and stronger than the gods, so that none could reach them. They also looked to "Rome" as the god who must be honored above all the gods.

The Greeks did not dare to attack the gods, whichever they were, but the Romans often pretended to honor even the strange gods of other peoples, yet they also mocked the gods and proclaimed their denial, reckoning that their state and their entity stood above every consideration.

"And at the time of the end shall the king of the south push at him: and the king of the north shall rise up against him with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall enter into the countries, and shall overflow and pass through.
He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many shall stumble: but these shall escape out of his hand, even Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.
He shall stretch forth his hand also upon the countries: and the land of Egypt shall not escape.
But he shall have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt:
and the Libyans and the Ethiopians shall be at his steps.
But tidings out of the east and out of the north shall trouble him: therefore he shall go forth with great fury to destroy, and utterly to make away many.

entries.section: 4. The end of times - the Antichrist:

paragraphs.text: And he shall plant the tabernacles of his palace between the seas and the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and none shall help him" [40-45]. [40-45] presents to us some events of the last days of the self-exalting king and others.
It is noted that it presents to us three persons: 1. The self-exalting king, "the Antichrist". 2. The king of the south (Egypt). 3. The king of the north (Syria).

St. Jerome says: [We read that Antiochus fulfilled this in part, but when we note what follows in detail, "and the Libyans (Libyans) and the Ethiopians (Ethiopians) shall be at his steps", our school insists that this suits the Antichrist more. For Antiochus never conquered Libya, which most writers understand as North Africa, nor Ethiopia].

entries.section: 4. The end of times - the Antichrist:

paragraphs.text: The Antichrist will set up his headquarters in Jerusalem, and his dominion will extend to the seas [45], especially the Mediterranean Sea and the Dead Sea. He will set up his headquarters on the glorious holy mountain, that is, Mount Zion. And with all the power and authority he attains, no one will be able to support him; the Antichrist will collapse before Elijah and Enoch, who support the Church in his time and prepare the believers for the final coming of the Lord Christ.
St. Jerome says: [Our school of thought insists that the Antichrist will perish at the very place where the Lord ascended to heaven (the Mount of Olives)].
Let history pass, and let the last times come!
* All history is in Your grasp, and nothing is hidden from You.
Mighty men arise and others collapse.
Covenants are made, some keep them, and others break them.
Kingdom wrestles with kingdom, and history folds up this one and that.
* Let history pass and be folded up with all its events, and let the last times come.
The Antichrist will pour out all his poisons; but our victorious Christ is surely coming!
Come, O Victor, and let Your believers be glorified!

1 And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time:
and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book. [1].

Since the chapter opens with the expression "And at that time" [1], it is clear that it continues what is stated in the previous chapter. For at the peak of the Antichrist's power the archangel Michael arises and works on behalf of the Church [as it is written in (Rev 12)], and this is in the period of the great tribulation that the Lord Christ announces (Mt 24:15-22).

In the midst of the tribulation God delivers the people of Daniel, that is, the Church of the believers whose names are written in the book of life. It is constantly exposed to tribulation, but it is not forgotten before God; rather, the more the tribulation intensifies, the more God shows His care for it. It is in the hand of its Savior the Lord Christ, who works for its building up, and uses His angels and archangels to protect it.

2 And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. 3 And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever. [2-3].

Some consider the Book of Daniel to be the first book of the Old Testament to speak clearly and strongly about the resurrection and to determine its time. When the great day of the Lord comes, the wise who obeyed God will shine like eternal stars. Yet this matter was reckoned beyond the ability of Daniel himself, for he says: "And I heard, but I understood not" [8].

Some try to distinguish here between two resurrections, one for the millennial reign and the other for eternal life, but it is clear that the talk here is of one resurrection and an eternal judgment, and eternal glory or torment.

* But those lords and teachers who have knowledge of the Law will shine like the heaven, and those who urge the peoples that lag behind in faith to give heed to the worship of God will glitter like stars in eternity.

St. Jerome * Let us flee with all our strength from the hindrances of this world and seek some hours in which we can devote ourselves to prayer or the reading of the Holy Bible for the salvation of our souls. This fulfills in us what is written: "And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament".

Fr. Caesarius * After the Antichrist is shattered and destroyed by the breath of the Savior's mouth, the people written in the book of God will be saved, each according to his merit; some will arise to everlasting life, and others to everlasting shame.

Teachers are likened to the very heavens, and those who teach others are compared to the brightness of the stars. For it is not enough for a person to know wisdom, but it is fitting for him to teach it to others.
The tongue of teaching that remains silent and edifies no one receives no reward.
St. Jerome * The Lord helps the humble, and the humble are changed into stars. For "the righteous shall shine as the stars", as Daniel says.
St. Jerome

4 But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall peruse it, and knowledge shall be increased. 5 Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river. 6 And one said to the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, How long shall it be to the end of these wonders? 7 And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, and two times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished. 8 And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things? 9 And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end. 10 Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand. 11 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. 12 Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. 13 But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.
"But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end:
many shall peruse it, and knowledge shall be increased" [4].

Daniel was commanded to seal the book, even "to the time of the end", but knowledge shall be increased, although a person remains as in a riddle until what is stated in the book is fully realized. Perhaps by the sealing here is meant that the prophecies remain unclear until salvation is accomplished in the fullness of the times, and the mysteries of the Second Coming are uncovered as in the Book of Revelation (Rev 22:10). For this reason many scholars see that the Book of Revelation is the key to the Book of Daniel.

St. Irenaeus sees that the divine inspiration asked Daniel to seal the prophecy, because no one could grasp it until the Lord Christ came, who is the goal of the prophecies, and then the believers would grasp its mystery, for he says: [The treasure hidden in the Holy Scriptures is Christ, to whom reference is made through types and parables. And since His human nature could not be understood before these predicted things were fulfilled, that is, before the coming of Christ, therefore it was said to Daniel the prophet: "Shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end, that many may learn and knowledge be perfected. At that time, when the dispensation is accomplished, they shall know all these things" (cf. Dan 12:4, 7). For every prophecy, before its fulfillment, is a riddle and an obscurity to men. But when the time comes and the prophecies are fulfilled, they become clear and their interpretation becomes certain].

St. Hippolytus of Rome says: [The things that were spoken in ancient times through the Law and the Prophets were all sealed, and were not known to men; Isaiah declares this by saying: "the sealed book, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed" (Isa 29:11). It is fitting and necessary that the things spoken by the prophets in ancient times should be sealed to the unbelieving Pharisees, who thought they understood the letter of the Law, while they are unsealed to the believers. The ancient things were sealed, but now by the grace of the Lord God all of them are unsealed to the saints. For He Himself (God) was the seal and the Church is the key: "he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth", as John says (Rev 3:7)... For this reason the angel says to Daniel: "Seal the words, for the vision is until the time of the end". But of Christ it is not said "seal", but rather He loosed the things that had been bound in ancient times, that by His grace the will of the Father may be known, and we may believe in Him whom He sent for the salvation of men, our Lord Jesus].

St. Jerome says [He who declared the truth in many ways to Daniel declares that the things He said are secret. And He asked him to roll up the scroll containing His words, and to put a seal on the book. The result is that many read it and ask about its fulfillment through history, and differ in their opinions (interpretations) because of its great obscurity.
By saying "many shall peruse it" [4], or "pass through it", he indicates that many read it...

And also in the Revelation of John a book is seen sealed within and without. And since no one could be found worthy to loose its seals, John says: "And I wept much... and a voice came to me: Weep not much, behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof" (cf. Rev 5:4).

But that book can be opened by one who learns the mysteries of the Scripture and understands its hidden truths and its words that seem dark because of the greatness of the mysteries they contain. It is he who is able to explain the parables and to turn the letter that kills into the Spirit that gives life.
St. Jerome "Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river.
And one said to the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river,
How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?

And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, and two times, and an half.
And when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.
And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things?
And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end.
Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried;
but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand" [5-10].

In order that Daniel might seal the book, he saw two other angels and the one clothed in linen, that is, the Word of God before the Incarnation (Dan 6:10). One of the angels asked him about the duration of this tribulation, and the answer came: for a time, and two times, and a half, that is, three and a half years. This is half of the week of which Daniel spoke before, a period of very bitter persecution, ending with the breaking of the covenant of the predatory king. St. Jerome says: [The time, and two times, and a half cannot be meant as the three and a half years in which Antiochus defiled the Temple, as Porphyry claimed, because this would require that the victor enjoy an eternal kingdom, and that all the kings submit to him and obey him, and this did not happen. Rather it is clear that the talk here is about the Antichrist, who reigns for 1290 days or three and a half years.

Although Daniel was asked to seal the book, because it contains mysteries that not everyone knows, and although Daniel himself says: "And I heard, but I understood not" [8], yet at the same time he affirms that whoever is pure and sanctified will understand what was said and become wise, while the wicked will not understand. Knowledge and wisdom here are relative matters; without doubt Daniel perceived much of the mysteries of the end of the age, but as in a mirror, or through the shadow, yet knowledge increases for the believers and many things are uncovered.

* He remarked that when the end comes the wicked will lack understanding, while those instructed in the teachings of God will be able to understand. For wisdom will not enter a perverse soul, nor can it disclose itself to a body subject to sins.
St. Jerome "And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.
Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days" [11-12].

He determines the period in days and not years, 1290 days, which means three and a half years, in which the Church suffers severe tribulation, with 45 days added to it (1335 days), and perhaps this period is the one between the killing of the Antichrist and the coming of the Lord Christ. It is a period of rest for the one who was led astray after the Antichrist to return and repent, and at the same time a period of purification for the believers, who await with joy the coming of Christ after deliverance from the Antichrist. Therefore Daniel the prophet pronounces blessed him that waiteth and cometh to the 1335 days.

St. Jerome says: [It is clear that the three and a half years were accepted with regard to the time of the Antichrist, for he will persecute the saints for three and a half years or 1290 days, and then he will face his fall on the famous holy mountain. Thus from the time at which he prevents the Endelekismos, which is translated "the perpetual sacrifice", that is, from the time at which the Antichrist reigns over the world and prevents the worship of God until the day of his death, the three and a half years or the 1290 days are completed].

* By this he means that blessed is he who waits forty-five days after the specified number (1290), for in this period our Lord will come in His glory. But the reason for the forty-five days after the killing of the Antichrist is a matter settled in the knowledge of God, unless we say that the judgment of the saints is postponed so that their faith may be tested. (by the final coming of Christ).
St. Jerome "But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days" [13].
Finally he asks Daniel to rest until he arises when the Lord of glory comes, who says, "Behold, I come quickly" (Rev 22).
* From this remark it appears clearly that the whole text of the prophecy concerns the resurrection of all the dead, the time at which the prophet too will arise.

St. Jerome In the sixteenth century John Calvin says that some commentators add the two numbers together (1290 + 1335), making about 2600 years, and since the prophecy dates from about 600 BC, the coming of the Lord Christ with the end of the world would be 2000 years after His first coming. Calvin rejected this interpretation.

And some comment on the saying of the Lord Christ in the parable of "the Good Samaritan": "And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee" (Lk 10:35), using the symbolic interpretation, that the Lord Christ has entrusted the wounded souls in this world into the hands of the militant Church for a period of 2000 years. For one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, so the two pence represent two thousand years after the ministry of Christ, that is, the Lord Christ returns, as it were, to the inn at the beginning of the twenty-first century.

His Grace Anba Dioscorus presented a study on the Book of Daniel in which he reveals the nearness of the end of the world, and opinions have also appeared in the West supporting the speedy end of the world. Some scientists have also seen that the widening of the ozone hole, from the scientific side, caused the movement of a huge mass of ice in the South Pole region over a distance of about 3 kilometers, and that its movement at this rate will lead to an imbalance in the magnetism and equilibrium of the earth, causing strong earthquakes and volcanoes that end in the destruction of the earth a few years after the year 2000.

The appearance of these opinions had strong repercussions in the East and the West, between supporters and opponents. But without doubt, when the "Antichrist" appears, the believers will discover that what is stated in the Book of Daniel was quite clear to the pious, just as the Church of the New Testament realized from the beginning of its launch, with the pious among the Jews, that the times relating to the coming of Christ were explicit and clear.

What I wish to make clear here is that since the Ascension of the Lord Christ the Church has been joyfully awaiting His quick coming, in the certainty that He is coming, and coming quickly, yet without disregard for temporal obligations and without slackness. The Lord Christ revealed to her the sure signs of His coming so that she might prepare with patience and face the tribulations, especially the great tribulation and His abomination of desolation, and also prepare with joy and hope that she has a share with Him in the Father's embrace. But now many think that awaiting the coming of the Lord Christ is regarded as a gloomy, pessimistic outlook that leads to slackness and negligence in fulfilling responsibilities; this reveals weakness of faith and the lack of hearts being kindled by the eschatological, heavenly thought.
He is surely coming! And the times will pass swiftly, and we will rejoice and exult in our resurrection with the dead, and our meeting with Him on the clouds.
Yes! Let the times pass away!
* For our sake You created time that we might glorify You in it, and for our sake time passes away that we might be glorified with You eternally.
Yes! Let the times pass away!
Come, O Beloved, to us, or carry us by Your Holy Spirit to You; we are hastening to meet You!
* Open the eyes of our hearts, that we may see You coming now into our depths, and see our souls passing over to You, enjoying Your presence!
